gaps.term: single route of a role through mixing gates
gaps.quote: Take an input role $w$ and its route to output role $\rho(w)$
gaps.note: Gates combine p inputs, so a role's value reaches the outputs along many paths, not one route. The page never says why the net map from role w is a single route whose telescoped operator, times the sign, gives the whole output at rho(w). It also never says why contributions along other paths cancel. The reader cannot check the formula 'by the telescoping' alone.

gaps.quote: Undoing the exchange moves each output back to its input role
gaps.note: The page never says how the exchange is undone: by a second run of the network, by its inverse, or by relabelling the role streams. It also never says why that operation exists or what it costs, so the reader cannot follow this step.

gaps.quote: multiplying by $-\varepsilon_w$ again removes the sign
gaps.note: Since epsilon_w is +1 or -1, multiplying epsilon_w by -epsilon_w gives -1, which flips the sign rather than removing it. The reader cannot see why -epsilon_w, and not epsilon_w, restores the original sign.

gaps.term: every role keeps the endpoint operator
gaps.quote: Every role keeps the endpoint operator (cited), auxiliary roles included.
gaps.note: This cited claim stands in for the page's own conclusion, but the page does not say what 'keeps the endpoint operator' means or why it holds. The reader cannot tell whether a scratch role ends up exactly restored or transformed by D_sink D_source^{-1}. The second reading conflicts with the opening promise that the network restores every auxiliary value.
